A **ICAO**, no Anexo 1, usa três classes: **ICAO**, in Annex 1, uses three classes. **Class 1** applies to commercial, multi-crew and airline transport licences; **Class 2**, to private, glider and balloon pilots, flight navigators and flight engineers; **Class 3**, to air traffic controllers and remote pilots. Flight attendants have no class in Annex 1: Brazil placed them in Class 2. The logic is the same in both systems: the more people depend on the body of the person flying, the stricter the examination (See M3V1 - III).
**Como prevenir e amenizar.** Antes do e: **How to prevent and ease it.** Before the examination, crew members book the appointment well ahead of expiry, bring their reports and medicine list and declare everything that has changed since the last examination. Between examinations, RBAC 67 and Annex 1 require crew not to fly when aware of a **decrease in medical fitness** and to inform ANAC or the examiner, especially after surgery, hospital admission, a new regular medicine or pregnancy (See M3V1 - II). Passengers do not need a certificate: their decision to fly goes through their own doctor and, when the airline asks, the medical form (MEDIF).
O que cada sistema do corpo precisa most: What must each body system show to receive the medical certificate in each class, and what makes an applicant unfit or fit with a limitation?
O **RBAC 67** organiza os requisitos por: **RBAC 67** organises requirements by body system, in the same order in each class: mind, nervous system, heart, lungs, digestive system, metabolism, blood, kidneys, pregnancy, bones, ear and nose, eyes, hearing and teeth. The examiner reaches one of three decisions: **fit**, **fit with a limitation**, with the conditions written in the certificate's remarks field, or **unfit**, with the right to appeal to ANAC. They take into account the role, the treatment available and the prognosis, and may find unfit someone with an unlisted condition that affects safety, provided this is justified in a report (See M3V1 - I).
A **validade** conta de dois jeitos. Na: **Validity** is counted in two ways. At first issue, or when the certificate has expired or been suspended, it runs from the date of the examination. When a still-valid certificate is revalidated up to **45 days** before expiry, the new period starts at the previous expiry date, so the crew member loses no days. Anyone whose certificate has been expired for more than **5 years** must take the initial examination again. A higher-class certificate is valid in place of a lower one, but moving up a class requires an initial examination. Between examinations, anyone who notices a **decrease in medical fitness** must inform ANAC or the examiner and stop flying until a new assessment.
Na **mente** e no **sistema nervoso**, a: In the **mind** and **nervous system**, the list is almost the same in every class. A history of organic mental disorder, substance use, schizophrenia, mood, anxiety and personality disorders makes an applicant unfit, as do epilepsy, stroke, aneurysm, haemorrhage and brain tumour. **Depression** treated with an antidepressant makes an applicant unfit unless the psychiatrist, with the details of the case, considers flying safe. Recurrent, unexplained **loss of consciousness** makes an applicant unfit; a single episode is judged by the examiner together with ANAC. The **electroencephalogram** is part of the initial examination for Classes 1, 2 and 5, and an EEG with slowing still allows the certificate if brain MRI shows no lesion (See M2V6 and M2V7).
No **coração**, tornam inapto na 1ª, na: In the **heart**, angina, valve disease, a pacemaker, a valve prosthesis, anticoagulants and blood pressure persistently above **140/90 mmHg** make an applicant unfit in Classes 1, 2 and 5, although antihypertensive treatment may be accepted. After a **heart attack**, pilots only return after **1 year**, with normal Holter, perfusion scan, echocardiogram and cholesterol and a favourable psychiatric opinion; after **angioplasty or bypass** without a heart attack, after **180 days**. In both cases, the decision is **fit with a limitation**, with validity of no more than **6 months**. The electrocardiogram with treadmill test is done at the initial examination and, in Class 1, every year from 50 and every 2 years from 30 to 49 (See M2V2).
No **metabolismo**, a diabetes tratada c: In **metabolism**, diabetes treated with **insulin** makes an applicant unfit in Classes 1, 2 and 5. So does blood glucose below **50** or above **140 mg/dL**, confirmed twice; between 50 and 69 or between 115 and 139, the examiner decides. On an oral antidiabetic, the applicant may be fit after **60 days** of observation with glucose between 70 and 139 mg/dL, and a pilot's certificate is valid for no more than 6 months. A **BMI** of 40 or more makes an applicant unfit in Classes 1 and 2. In the blood, a coumarin anticoagulant makes an applicant unfit, and sickle-cell trait is accepted if there is no risk of a crisis in flight. **Asthma** makes an applicant unfit in Classes 1, 2 and 5, and a transplanted kidney may be accepted in consultation with ANAC (See M2V9, M2V11 and M2V14).
Nos **olhos**, a 1ª classe pede **20/30*: In the **eyes**, Class 1 requires **20/30** in each eye and **20/20** with both, plus reading at near and at 1 metre; Classes 2 and 5 require 20/40 in each eye and 20/30 with both, and a private pilot with an instrument rating follows Class 1. Lenses are accepted, with spare glasses, and refractive surgery after 6 months. In **hearing**, audiometry accepts a loss of up to **35 dB** at 500, 1,000 and 2,000 Hz and **50 dB** at 3,000 Hz; anyone who fails may still receive the certificate with the limitation of not flying where radio is required. In **pregnancy**, Classes 1 and 2 make the applicant unfit from confirmation; Class 4 accepts a low-risk pregnancy between the **12th and 26th week**, and Class 5 up to the **34th week** (See M2V3, M2V4 and M2V13).
**Como prevenir e amenizar.** Antes do e: **How to prevent and ease it.** Before the examination, crew members check the requirements for their class, have the laboratory and imaging tests requested and bring the reports of the specialists who follow any chronic condition. They book revalidation up to 45 days before expiry, so as not to lose days of validity. They look after what most often takes pilots off flying: blood pressure, sugar, weight, cholesterol, sleep and mental health, and treat problems early. After surgery, hospital admission, a new medicine or pregnancy, they inform ANAC or the examiner before returning to flying. The examiner records on the certificate each limitation and what the applicant must meet to work.

Entre um exame e outro, a responsabilida: Between examinations, responsibility lies with the person who flies. Annex 1 forbids exercising the licence when holders are aware of a **decrease in medical fitness** that could compromise safety, and RBAC 67 requires them to inform ANAC or the examiner and stop flying until a new assessment. The FAA forbids flying while knowing of a condition that would prevent certification or while using medicine that causes it. Europe lists when to see the examiner **without undue delay**: surgery or an invasive procedure, starting a regular medicine, significant injury or illness, pregnancy, hospital admission and the first need for lenses. Flying while hiding the condition puts the body at risk on board and may cost the licence, the insurance and the career.
Risco aceito porque o segundo piloto ass: Risk accepted because the second pilot takes over if the first fails (See M3V1 - V)
Erros dos dois lados custam caro. O trip: Mistakes on either side are costly. A crew member who flies with a hidden condition risks fainting, arrhythmia or a wrong decision at the controls, besides losing insurance cover and, after an accident, facing the investigation. In Brazil, anyone who flies in a condition prohibited by RBAC 67 has the certificate revoked and may only apply again after **180 days**; omitting information also leads to revocation, and fraud to a wait of at least **12 months** and a report to the Public Prosecutor's Office. An examiner who misses a finding or issues outside the rules may lose the designation and answer to the authority and the medical council. That is why, when in doubt, the examiner **defers** and asks for reports instead of deciding alone.
A restrição mais usada para manter algué: The limitation most used to keep someone flying with a risk slightly above the limit is to fly **only with another qualified pilot**. It uses the same reasoning as the calculation: if the first pilot fails, the second takes over, and the risk that reaches the passenger falls a hundredfold. That is why a pilot with a treated, stable and monitored condition can keep flying, as long as never alone at the controls, while treatment and follow-up tests show the risk has not risen (See M3V1 - III).
O número tem limites. Ele depende de est: The figure has limits. It depends on estimating each person's risk, and risk calculators were built for the general population: in New Zealand, screening based on them missed more than half of the pilots who had an event. The calculation also captures **subtle incapacitation** poorly, such as fatigue, medicine effects and mental illness, which do not switch the pilot off at once but worsen decision-making. That is why aerospace medicine began to seek each person's own risk (See M3V1 - VI).
A **medicina de precisão** troca a pergu: **Precision medicine** swaps the question "does this pilot meet the standard?" for "what is the risk in this body, and what lowers it?". It uses each person's history, family, tests and course over time to decide who needs further investigation, who can fly with a limitation and who can fly with none. Annex 1 itself asks States to analyse in-flight incapacitation events, reassess the rules with those data and promote the health of those who fly (See M3V1 - III).
Nem todo exame serve para isso. O **test: Not every test serves this purpose. The **exercise test** alone has a sensitivity of only 60% to 70% for coronary disease and predicts events poorly, so it should not be used as the only test, although it remains useful to measure fitness and the blood-pressure response. **Ischaemia** tests come after imaging, as second line. A normal perfusion scan works as a "warranty": the risk of a significant event stays below **1% per year** for about **3 years** (See M3V1 - V).
A outra frente é a **mente**. Depois do: The other front is the **mind**. After the 2015 accident in the Alps, Europe began requiring **peer support**, in which trained pilots confidentially support colleagues in distress, as well as a psychological assessment before line flying and alcohol testing. Precision here means finding early who needs help and treating without punishing, because a pilot who fears losing the licence hides the symptom, and it is untreated illness that reaches the cockpit as a danger (See M2V7 and M3V1 - IV).
